hypotheses.claim: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomic profiling (fragment size, copy-number, nucleosome patterns) via low-pass whole-genome sequencing can non-invasively detect biliary tract cancer, including at earlier or resectable stages, better than single-analyte markers.
hypotheses.reasoning: A dedicated model-development/validation study applied fragmentomics to BTC detection and risk stratification. The same review on GI liquid biopsy also cautions that sensitivity for stage I disease remains limited across cancer types due to low tumor DNA shedding, tempering confidence for very early lesions.

hypotheses.claim: A history of chronic Opisthorchis viverrini or Clonorchis sinensis liver fluke infection identifies a high-risk population in whom targeted biomarker or imaging screening programs could enable earlier CCA detection.
hypotheses.reasoning: Multiple studies establish liver flukes as Group 1 carcinogens strongly linked to CCA in endemic Southeast/East Asia, supporting risk-stratified screening; however, persistent reinfection dynamics after treatment (shown in the Thai cohort) complicate defining a stable 'exposed' risk window for screening timing.

hypotheses.claim: A four-marker droplet-digital-PCR DNA methylation panel measured in bile (and to a lesser extent plasma) can accurately distinguish CCA from PSC alone, offering a practical liquid-biopsy triage test deployable during ERCP for high-risk PSC surveillance programs.
hypotheses.reasoning: A multi-hospital study using reduced representation bisulfite sequencing followed by ddPCR validation in 272 bile and 128 plasma samples identified four methylation biomarkers with improved accuracy for CCA detection in PSC patients versus current clinical methods; bile-based signal outperformed plasma, suggesting an ERCP-integrated triage assay is nearer-term than a pure blood test.

hypotheses.claim: Annual MRCP-based surveillance in patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) can identify cholangiocarcinoma earlier than symptom-triggered imaging, though its effect on mortality reduction remains incompletely proven in real-world cohorts.
hypotheses.reasoning: A retrospective cohort directly compared MRCP surveillance vs non-surveillance in PSC, providing an evidentiary basis, and a systematic review quantifies PSC prevalence/CCA risk to define the at-risk population. However, a case report of iCCA in small-duct PSC despite atypical MRCP appearance shows surveillance protocols may miss some at-risk phenotypes, motivating protocol refinement.

hypotheses.claim: Plasma ctDNA detection of hotspot IDH1 R132 mutations (e.g., R132C, more common than R132H in cholangiocarcinoma) can serve as a tumor-informed liquid biopsy marker for early detection and minimal residual disease monitoring in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, given documented tissue-plasma concordance.
hypotheses.reasoning: IDH1 mutations are clonal, early truncal events in a defined subset (~15-20%) of intrahepatic CCA, and ctDNA-tissue concordance has been demonstrated, supporting feasibility of blood-based detection; however, IDH1 mutations are absent in the majority of CCA cases, limiting sensitivity as a universal early-detection marker and restricting use to an IDH-mutant subgroup.

hypotheses.claim: Serum β-hCG (via LHCGR pathway upregulation) combined with conventional tumor markers (CA19-9, CEA) improves detection sensitivity for CCA over single-marker testing.
hypotheses.reasoning: A multi-omics discovery study identified LHCGR/β-hCG upregulation correlating with CCA stage and showed added value when combined with routine markers in a Thai cohort; this is a single-population, tissue+serum discovery study needing external validation before broad use.

hypotheses.claim: IDH1/IDH2 mutant ctDNA detected in plasma can serve as a tumor-informed biomarker for identifying molecular residual disease and potentially earlier recurrence in IDH-mutant intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, extending to earlier detection paradigms.
hypotheses.reasoning: Direct evidence shows strong concordance between tissue and plasma IDH1/2 mutations enabling molecular residual disease detection; CIViC evidence confirms IDH1 mutations are a validated, clinically actionable subtype in CCA, supporting biological plausibility for earlier molecular detection even though current use is post-resection surveillance rather than de novo screening.

hypotheses.claim: Pancreatobiliary FISH (PB-FISH) as part of multimodality tissue sampling improves detection of malignant biliary strictures, but a substantial false-negative rate limits its stand-alone use for early detection.
hypotheses.reasoning: A prospective study explicitly quantifies false-negative PB-FISH rates (40-50%) and identifies predictors, meaning it is a useful adjunct but not sufficiently sensitive alone — a self-contained conflicting/limiting finding from the same study.

hypotheses.claim: Targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) gene panels applied directly to ERCP transpapillary brushing/biopsy specimens can increase molecular diagnostic yield for biliary tract cancer beyond cytology/histology alone.
hypotheses.reasoning: A narrative review focused specifically on NGS applied to small transpapillary specimens, complemented by comprehensive genomic profiling studies identifying frequent TP53/KRAS/ARID1A/CDKN2A alterations that could serve as molecular adjuncts to cytology in indeterminate strictures.

hypotheses.claim: Plasma ctDNA methylation-based tests (e.g., HepaAiQ-like or BTC-specific assays) can detect biliary tract cancer non-invasively and are now being prospectively validated as screening tools in at-risk populations.
hypotheses.reasoning: An active clinical trial is specifically developing a cfDNA methylation blood test for BTC screening, and a review outlines ctDNA-guided early detection evidence and barriers in pancreatobiliary cancers; general liquid-biopsy literature nonetheless flags persistent limits in stage-I sensitivity.

hypotheses.claim: Combining CA19-9 with genomic mutation panels (KRAS, TP53, SMAD4, GNAS) on biliary brush cytology/bile improves sensitivity and specificity for detecting malignant biliary strictures compared to CA19-9 alone.
hypotheses.reasoning: CA19-9 alone lacks sensitivity/specificity for early CCA; multiple sources support that adding NGS-based mutation calling to conventional CA19-9/cytology substantially improves diagnostic yield for indeterminate strictures.

hypotheses.claim: Combining ctDNA detection with hybrid imaging-molecular surveillance frameworks after intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma resection could detect microscopic recurrence earlier than imaging alone, a paradigm potentially transferable to pre-diagnostic early detection.
hypotheses.reasoning: A proposed hybrid framework article and real-world bespoke ctDNA experience both argue imaging alone misses molecular residual disease; this is largely proposed/early real-world evidence rather than prospective randomized validation, so confidence is moderate.

hypotheses.claim: AI/deep learning-based radiomics applied to contrast-enhanced CT/MRI can improve differentiation of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma from other focal liver lesions (including HCC) at an earlier, potentially more resectable stage than conventional radiologic assessment alone.
hypotheses.reasoning: A systematic review/meta-analysis specifically quantifies radiomics/AI diagnostic performance for ICC detection and differentiation, supported by additional AI-in-liver-cancer reviews; heterogeneity in AI model validation across studies and lack of prospective screening-population data are inherent limitations noted in these reviews themselves.

hypotheses.claim: Multi-gene targeted NGS of ERCP-derived biliary brushings/bile fluid (e.g., Oncomine Comprehensive/Pan-Cancer cfDNA assays) outperforms cytology and FISH for detecting malignant strictures at an earlier, potentially curable stage.
hypotheses.reasoning: Prospective studies directly comparing NGS to cytohistology/FISH in biliary strictures show improved diagnostic performance, suggesting a route to earlier molecular diagnosis in patients under endoscopic surveillance, though sample adequacy and cost remain practical barriers.

hypotheses.claim: Serum β-hCG (via LHCGR/β-hCG axis) added to traditional tumor markers (CA19-9/CEA) improves detection efficacy and prognostic prediction for cholangiocarcinoma, representing a low-cost add-on blood test to existing panels.
hypotheses.reasoning: A multi-omics-driven study in a CCA-endemic population (Northeast Thailand) identified LHCGR upregulation and validated serum β-hCG as a translatable biomarker correlating with stage and improving detection when combined with routine markers; needs independent external validation given single-population origin.

hypotheses.claim: Advanced endoscopic sampling combining ERCP with cholangioscopy and confocal laser endomicroscopy (CLE) increases diagnostic yield for early/indeterminate biliary strictures compared to brush cytology alone.
hypotheses.reasoning: Multiple reviews and case reports support CLE/cholangioscopy improving real-time detection of early biliary adenocarcinoma; a comparative brush cytology vs biopsy study shows variable diagnostic accuracy ranges for standard sampling, underscoring the incremental value but also study heterogeneity.

hypotheses.claim: Metabolic syndrome, obesity, and type 2 diabetes mellitus are independent risk factors for cholangiocarcinoma (particularly intrahepatic subtype) and could inform risk-stratified screening in Western populations with rising incidence.
hypotheses.reasoning: Multiple independent epidemiologic studies (Korean cohort, Chinese case-control, cardiometabolic review) support metabolic risk factors for CCA; however, an editorial explicitly notes these are large studies with small absolute risk increases, limiting practical screening utility despite population-level significance.

hypotheses.claim: Genetic predisposition via cholelithiasis-associated loci and shared germline variants (e.g., LRPPRC, ABCG5) may identify a subgroup at elevated biliary tract cancer risk amenable to targeted early detection strategies.
hypotheses.reasoning: GWAS/Mendelian randomization studies link cholelithiasis genetic liability to increased extrahepatic CCA risk via shared loci; however, a separate two-sample MR study on cholecystitis specifically found no clear independent causal relationship with CCA, indicating the causal architecture is condition-specific and requires careful phenotype definition.

hypotheses.claim: Low-pass whole-genome cfDNA fragmentomics (fragment size distribution, copy-number variation, nucleosome positioning derived from a single low-cost sequencing run) can non-invasively detect biliary tract cancer and stratify postoperative risk, representing a scalable blood-based screening/monitoring approach.
hypotheses.reasoning: A model development/validation study specifically built and validated a low-pass WGS fragmentomics framework for BTC detection and risk assessment from plasma; as a genome-wide, low-depth-sequencing method it could be cheaper/more scalable than tumor-informed ctDNA panels, but independent validation in truly early/asymptomatic populations is still needed.

hypotheses.claim: Circulating exosome/extracellular vesicle cargo (proteins and miRNAs) reflects tumor-specific signatures detectable in blood and could complement or outperform CA19-9 for earlier, non-invasive CCA detection.
hypotheses.reasoning: Multiple reviews and a dedicated EV-guided multi-compartment biomarker prioritization framework support EV-based biomarker discovery for CCA; most work remains at cell-line/proof-of-concept stage without large clinical validation cohorts.

hypotheses.claim: A dedicated cholangiocarcinoma GWAS-defined polygenic risk profile (including HLA and other loci) could eventually stratify individuals, especially those with PSC, for enhanced surveillance intensity.
hypotheses.reasoning: A large European-ancestry GWAS of ~2,366 CCA cases identified genome-wide significant loci and PSC-stratified subgroup signals, and a related UK Biobank-derived TERT variant study links germline variation to incidence and prognosis; translation to a validated clinical risk score for screening remains preliminary.

hypotheses.claim: Targeted NGS panels detecting FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements in bile or biliary brushings can improve early discrimination of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma from benign strictures, since FGFR2 fusions are a recurrent, largely CCA-specific truncal alteration.
hypotheses.reasoning: FGFR2 fusions are enriched in intrahepatic CCA and are already used as molecular endoscopy targets in biliary brushings/NGS panels showing improved diagnostic yield over cytology/FISH alone; specificity for early neoplasia versus advanced disease still needs validation in asymptomatic/high-risk cohorts.

hypotheses.claim: Postoperative surveillance ctDNA (tumor-informed, tracking somatic variants identified in resected tumor tissue) can detect molecular residual disease in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma earlier than radiographic recurrence, enabling a hybrid imaging-molecular early-recurrence-detection framework.
hypotheses.reasoning: Multiple sources propose and support tumor-informed ctDNA MRD detection as more sensitive than imaging for microscopic residual/recurrent disease in resected intrahepatic CCA, though prospective outcome-changing trials are still needed for adoption as standard early-recurrence surveillance.

hypotheses.claim: Molecular imaging using fluorescently labeled peptide dimers targeting EGFR and HER2 (biliary intraepithelial neoplasia biomarkers) during cholangioscopy could enable earlier in vivo detection of dysplastic/early neoplastic biliary epithelium not yet visible by standard endoscopy.
hypotheses.reasoning: An active Phase 1 feasibility trial is testing a dual-target (EGFR/HER2) fluorescent peptide dimer for cholangioscopic detection of biliary intraepithelial neoplasia, directly addressing tumor genetic heterogeneity; as an early-phase feasibility study, clinical performance data are not yet available.

hypotheses.claim: Persistently elevated serum gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) in the general population is associated with increased incident risk of hepatobiliary malignancies, including cholangiocarcinoma, and could serve as a low-cost trigger for further work-up.
hypotheses.reasoning: A large propensity-matched TriNetX cohort study directly links persistently elevated GGT to hepatobiliary cancer outcomes; as GGT is nonspecific (elevated in alcohol use, metabolic disease), it would function only as a low-specificity trigger rather than standalone diagnostic.

hypotheses.claim: Metformin use is associated with reduced risk of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma among individuals with diabetes, suggesting a chemopreventive avenue that could shift population risk and inform who should be prioritized for surveillance.
hypotheses.reasoning: A nationwide Swedish population-based cohort study using anti-diabetic medication dispensing data found associations between metformin use and reduced liver cancer risk including intrahepatic CCA; single-country observational data warrants replication before altering screening/prevention paradigms.

hypotheses.claim: Bile-derived exosomal microRNAs miR-196a and miR-196b are elevated in biliary tract cancer, including early-stage disease, and could serve as a minimally invasive diagnostic panel obtainable during ERCP.
hypotheses.reasoning: A validated two-cohort study (screening + independent validation, n=103) shows miR-196a/196b elevated in bile exosomes of BTC patients including early-stage cases with reported AUROC ~0.79, though this requires validation against benign biliary strictures/inflammation as important confounders.

hypotheses.claim: Serum/plasma clusterin (CLU), identified via bile proteomics and validated as a blood/bile biomarker, combined with a deep-learning diagnostic model, is a promising near-term liquid biomarker for CCA diagnosis deployable as a multi-analyte assay.
hypotheses.reasoning: A two-center study of 644 subjects identified and validated clusterin as a novel bile/serum marker with an online deep-learning prediction platform, and subsequent reviews list clusterin among emerging liquid-biopsy analytes for CCA; validation across broader, more diverse and truly early-stage cohorts is still needed.

hypotheses.claim: Serum clusterin (CLU), identified via bile/serum proteomics, may function as a novel diagnostic biomarker for cholangiocarcinoma with potential utility in earlier non-invasive detection when combined with deep-learning multi-analyte models.
hypotheses.reasoning: A two-center proteomics study (644 subjects) identified and validated bile/serum clusterin with a deep-learning diagnostic model; this is a promising but single-source discovery finding requiring independent external replication before adoption for early detection.

hypotheses.claim: Bile-based ctDNA analysis (KRAS/TP53 and other hotspot mutations) obtained during ERCP shows higher concordance with tumor tissue than plasma ctDNA and could serve as an adjunct molecular test for indeterminate biliary strictures.
hypotheses.reasoning: Reviews report bile ctDNA has superior concordance with tumor tissue relative to blood, and population-specific KRAS/CREBBP mutation signatures have been characterized in liver-fluke-associated CCA, supporting bile-based mutation testing as a practical adjunct to brush cytology during ERCP in patients already undergoing the procedure for stricture evaluation.

hypotheses.claim: Non-targeted bile and serum metabolomic profiling can distinguish cholangiocarcinoma from benign biliary conditions (e.g., recurrent choledocholithiasis) and from PSC, offering a novel diagnostic adjunct obtainable during routine ERCP.
hypotheses.reasoning: A dedicated LC-MS bile metabolomics study directly compared CCA, primary and recurrent choledocholithiasis, and a separate blood metabolomic test development effort targets PSC/CCA discrimination; both are early-stage discovery studies in modest single-center cohorts.

hypotheses.claim: Sugar-sweetened beverage consumption is associated with increased risk of liver cancer including intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, representing a modifiable dietary exposure that could refine risk stratification for early surveillance candidacy.
hypotheses.reasoning: A large pooled analysis of 11 prospective cohorts specifically examined beverage intake and liver cancer subtype risk including ICC, providing solid epidemiologic support, though the strength/specificity of the ICC-specific association versus HCC needs further scrutiny.

hypotheses.claim: KRAS mutation detection (particularly G12D/G12V allelic variants) in bile, biliary brushings, or plasma ctDNA can flag high-risk biliary strictures and early biliary tract cancer, especially in liver-fluke-associated or Western populations with 20-30% KRAS-mutant prevalence.
hypotheses.reasoning: KRAS mutations occur in 20-30% of biliary tract cancers and are detectable by NGS in bile/brushings; however KRAS mutations also occur in benign/reactive pancreatobiliary epithelium and IPMN, raising specificity concerns for a false-positive-prone standalone marker.

hypotheses.claim: Persistently elevated serum CA19-9 (beyond levels explained by benign cholestasis) in an at-risk individual (e.g., PSC, biliary stricture) is a practical, low-cost triage signal warranting imaging/further workup for cholangiocarcinoma, though its poor specificity and Lewis-antigen-dependent expression limit standalone screening use.
hypotheses.reasoning: CA19-9 is the most widely used clinical marker in CCA workups; it is elevated in advanced CCA cohorts and used in corrected/nomogram models, but the IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis case report shows very high CA19-9 (315 U/mL) in a benign mimic, underscoring poor specificity and the need for combination approaches rather than CA19-9 alone.

hypotheses.claim: A serum panel combining CA19-9 with CEA (and often CA125) improves discrimination of malignant vs benign biliary disease compared to any single marker, and is a practical near-term triage tool since all three assays are routinely available in clinical labs.
hypotheses.reasoning: Multiple reviews and cohort studies note CEA/CA19-9 elevation as classic CCA laboratory features, and combination panels are repeatedly proposed to offset the low sensitivity/specificity of any single legacy marker, though liquid biopsy reviews caution these markers remain inadequate for early-stage screening on their own.

hypotheses.claim: A recombinant liver-fluke antigen-based (P9-IgG4) point-of-care immunochromatographic test can identify Opisthorchis viverrini infection and infection-associated cholangiocarcinoma risk in endemic populations, providing a field-deployable, low-cost triage tool for community-level risk stratification and referral for imaging surveillance.
hypotheses.reasoning: An immunomics-guided study specifically developed and validated P9-IgG4 point-of-care immunochromatographic tests in endemic sera, outperforming crude-antigen IgG tests for both fluke infection and infection-associated CCA; a companion review notes most such molecular/serologic biomarkers remain in early-stage small-cohort research without large multi-center prospective validation.

hypotheses.claim: MRI-based pharmacokinetic modeling of quantitative liver function (as opposed to conventional static MRCP reading) is a promising non-invasive imaging biomarker for risk-stratifying PSC patients for adverse outcomes including cholangiocarcinoma, potentially enabling risk-adapted surveillance intervals.
hypotheses.reasoning: A prospective pilot study of 26 PSC patients followed for up to 7.5 years found pharmacokinetic MRI-derived liver function measures correlated with clinical endpoints including cholangiocarcinoma; small pilot sample size and single-cohort design mean this needs larger validation before adoption as a surveillance tool.

hypotheses.claim: Bile-derived exosomal cargo (proteins/RNA) profiling can outperform serum CA19-9 for early, localized cholangiocarcinoma detection because bile is in direct anatomical proximity to the tumor, concentrating tumor-derived vesicles.
hypotheses.reasoning: Multiple reviews support proximity-based enrichment rationale for bile-based liquid biopsy, and bile exosomal miRNA data show promising AUROC values; however comparative head-to-head trials against CA19-9 in early-stage cohorts are limited.

hypotheses.claim: Serial serum biobanking (annual MRCP plus paired serum/plasma) in prospectively followed primary sclerosing cholangitis cohorts provides a platform to discover and validate blood-based molecular biomarkers (mutational or epigenetic) that could enable earlier cholangiocarcinoma detection in this high-risk population.
hypotheses.reasoning: An active national Swedish PSC surveillance cohort (600 patients) with longitudinal serum/plasma biobanking and imaging is explicitly designed to enable biomarker discovery for early CCA detection in PSC, a population with a 6-13% lifetime CCA risk, representing a strong translational research platform though results are still pending.

hypotheses.claim: A comprehensive bile multi-omics profile (16S microbiome sequencing, metabolomics, bile-acid quantification) obtained during ERCP can distinguish CCA from PSC and benign biliary disease, providing a practical 'one-sample' add-on test at the time of endoscopic biliary sampling that is already part of standard care.
hypotheses.reasoning: Bile is already collected during ERCP for cytology, so adding microbiome/metabolomic/bile acid profiling is logistically practical; a dedicated multi-omics bile study found distinguishing microbial and metabolomic features by diagnosis, and bile acid-microbiome axis dysregulation is mechanistically linked to biliary carcinogenesis, though causal specificity for CCA vs. other cholestatic disease needs larger validation.

hypotheses.claim: A circulating microRNA panel (e.g., serum miR-302d-3p and related p53-pathway-linked miRNAs) can enhance diagnostic discrimination of CCA from healthy controls and may be developed into a low-cost RT-qPCR blood assay for at-risk populations.
hypotheses.reasoning: Two independent studies (small RNA sequencing plus RT-qPCR validation in serum, and Nanostring profiling of advanced iCCA) identified differentially expressed circulating miRNAs with diagnostic/prognostic value; sample sizes are modest and most studies to date profile symptomatic/advanced-stage patients rather than a true early-detection or asymptomatic screening cohort.

hypotheses.claim: Optical coherence tomography (volumetric laser endomicroscopy) can supplement ERCP-based tissue sampling to characterize indeterminate biliary strictures with higher resolution, aiding earlier distinction of malignant lesions obscured by stents or inflammation.
hypotheses.reasoning: A comprehensive review describes OCT/VLE capabilities in overcoming stent/inflammation artifacts for biliary duct evaluation, but notes the evidence base remains an emerging application without large validated outcome studies.

hypotheses.claim: GNAS activating mutations, when detected together with KRAS in bile duct cyst fluid or bile, can identify intraductal papillary neoplasms of the bile duct (IPNB) at a precancerous stage before progression to invasive cholangiocarcinoma, analogous to pancreatic IPMN surveillance.
hypotheses.reasoning: GNAS/KRAS mutation testing is an established strategy for pancreatic cystic precursor lesions (IPMN); analogous biliary precursor lesions (IPNB) are recognized pathologically, but direct evidence of GNAS-based bile fluid testing specifically for IPNB-to-CCA progression is still limited.

hypotheses.claim: Persistently elevated gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) on routine liver panels (>65 U/L on two occasions 6-12 months apart) is a real-world risk flag associated with increased incidence of hepatobiliary malignancies (including cholangiocarcinoma) and could be used as an inexpensive triage trigger for further hepatobiliary evaluation.
hypotheses.reasoning: A large real-world TriNetX cohort study with propensity matching found persistently elevated GGT associated with higher risk of hepatobiliary/pancreatic cancer outcomes; GGT is non-specific (also elevated with alcohol use, metabolic dysfunction) limiting specificity for CCA specifically.

hypotheses.claim: Circulating miRNA panels (e.g., miR-302d-3p and others identified via Nanostring profiling) differentiate CCA patients, including by metastatic status, and could be developed into an early, minimally invasive detection panel.
hypotheses.reasoning: A dedicated study profiled serum miRNAs across CCA disease stages using high-throughput Nanostring technology in a Thai cohort; the study was framed around prognosis in advanced-stage patients rather than early/localized disease, limiting direct evidence for early detection utility.

hypotheses.claim: MSI-High/dMMR status, though present in only a small subset of cholangiocarcinoma, can be used as a molecular flag prompting germline Lynch syndrome evaluation and enrollment into intensified early-detection surveillance protocols for at-risk relatives.
hypotheses.reasoning: dMMR/MSI-H CCA is documented, including cases arising in Lynch syndrome; while primarily framed as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy, its detection has cascade implications for identifying hereditary risk and could support earlier surveillance-based detection in mutation carriers rather than sporadic population screening.

hypotheses.claim: Promoter hypermethylation of tumor suppressor genes (e.g., CDKN2A/p16, RASSF1A) detected in bile or cfDNA can serve as an early epigenetic biomarker of cholangiocarcinocarcinogenesis, including in liver-fluke-associated disease.
hypotheses.reasoning: CDKN2A and RASSF1A hypermethylation are broadly documented pan-cancer early epigenetic events, and Opisthorchis viverrini-associated CCA shows a predominant hypermethylation phenotype; however, most supporting studies are in liver-fluke-endemic cohorts and lack large-scale prospective validation.

hypotheses.claim: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs), particularly mesenchymal-phenotype CTCs identified via EMT markers, could serve as an adjunct early/prognostic detection tool in cholangiocarcinoma, reflecting tumor burden and invasive potential.
hypotheses.reasoning: CTC/VCTC counts correlate with tumor size, stage, and metastasis in a large cohort (n=149), but current data are drawn from patients with established diagnoses of varying stages rather than asymptomatic/high-risk screening populations, so evidence for true 'early' detection utility is indirect.

hypotheses.claim: Clonorchis sinensis and Opisthorchis viverrini infection-associated epigenetic/miRNA/metabolite signatures could be used as population-specific pre-neoplastic biomarkers to identify high-risk individuals for intensified cholangiocarcinoma surveillance in endemic liver-fluke regions.
hypotheses.reasoning: Multiple reviews document parasite-driven epigenetic and miRNA changes preceding overt CCA in fluke-endemic regions, supporting a risk-stratification rationale; however, the same sources note research remains largely lab-stage with small, non-multicenter cohorts lacking prospective validation.

hypotheses.claim: Chronic hepatitis B virus infection and virus-associated cirrhosis are practical, testable risk markers (via existing HBsAg/HBV DNA serology already used in liver clinics) that should prompt closer imaging surveillance for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, given documented HBV-iCCA co-occurrence and synergism with diabetes.
hypotheses.reasoning: Population case-control data show HBV infection as an independent CCA risk factor with synergistic interaction with diabetes; multiple case reports document iCCA arising in HBV-infected livers (sometimes confused with recurrent HCC), supporting use of existing HBV serology as an inexpensive risk-stratification tool, though most HBV patients do not develop CCA (low absolute risk).

In PDAC, progress includes refinement of perioperative management, broader germline and somatic testing, recognition of DNA damage repair-deficient subsets, and development of KRAS-directed therapies and rational combination strategies. PMID:42136955.title: Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma in Small-Duct Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis Associated With Crohn Disease: First Reported Case and Surveillance Implications.
PMID:42136955.snippet: Small-duct primary sclerosing cholangitis (sd-PSC) is traditionally regarded as a milder variant of PSC with a lower risk of hepatobiliary malignancy. Its association with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) remains unexplored. A 61-year-old woman with newly diagnosed Crohn disease presented with weight loss, anemia, and a liver mass initially suspected as hepatocellular carcinoma; biopsy confirmed poorly differentiated iCCA (CK7+/CK19+/Arginase-). MRCP showed normal large ducts with focal intrahepatic dilatation; liver biopsy demonstrated periductal onion-skin fibrosis diagnostic of sd-PSC. This report documents the first instance of metastatic iCCA in sd-PSC-CD, challenging current hepato-biliary malignancy surveillance paradigms in patients with inflammatory bowel disease.

Background

Annual surveillance for cholangiocarcinoma using magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) has been recommended in primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) to improve the associated dismal outcomes. However, data are limited.

PMID:42435161.title: Epidemiology of primary sclerosing cholangitis in general and IBD populations: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
PMID:42435161.snippet:
Background & aims

Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver condition that is closely associated with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). PSC is associated with substantial long-term hepatobiliary morbidity, including an increased risk of cholangiocarcinoma. Reported prevalence and incidence estimates of PSC vary widely across different populations and study designs. This meta-analysis aims to provide an updated estimate of the prevalence of PSC in the general and IBD populations, and PSC incidence in the general population.

PMID:42406772.title: Longitudinal changes and risk factors of Opisthorchis viverrini infection after selective praziquantel treatment: evidence from urine antigen assay and fecal examination in an endemic community in Northeast Thailand.
PMID:42406772.snippet: Opisthorchis viverrini infection remains an important public health problem in Southeast Asia, particularly among rural populations in Northeast Thailand. Despite control efforts, transmission remains uninterrupted due to persistent behavioral and environmental factors. To better understand the longitudinal patterns of opisthorchiasis after selective praziquantel treatment, this study aimed to determine the incidence and reinfection rates in the study population and identify risk factors associated with O. viverrini infection. PMID:42185667.snippet: Helminth infections remain a major public health problem in the Lao People's Democratic Republic (Lao PDR), particularly in rural communities where foodborne trematodes and soil-transmitted helminths are co-endemic. Opisthorchis viverrini is a well-established risk factor for cholangiocarcinoma, while Strongyloides stercoralis can cause severe and potentially fatal disease. PMID:42032916.title: Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma Surgery Outcomes and Survival Factors in an Opisthorchis viverrini -Endemic Area.
PMID:42032916.snippet:
Background

Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a malignancy of the bile duct epithelium. Its incidence is highest in Northeast Thailand, where it is strongly associated with Opisthorchis viverrini (OV) infection. The only curative treatment for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (IHCCA), the most common subtype, is surgical resection. This study aimed to investigate survival outcomes and identify factors associated with long-term survival in resectable IHCCA patients in the high-incidence of OV infection.

Methods

PMID:42221312.title: The role of liver fluke invasion in the pathogenesis of cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:42221312.snippet: Infections with the liver flukes Clonorchis sinensis and Opisthorchis viverrini are currently endemic in Southeast and East Asia. Their limited ecological and geographical distribution is caused by environmental factors and culinary habits of the human population. Climate change, globalization, increasing human mobility, and environmental changes affecting the reservoir of zoonotic infections may change the epidemiology of trematodes. The species C. sinensis and O. viverrini have been recognized as biological carcinogens leading to the development of biliary tract cancer. This paper presents the epidemiology of infections with the above species, and summarizes the known mechanisms of cholangiocarcinogenesis induced by parasitic invasion.

PMID:40937874.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Congenital Biliary Dilatation Surgery: A Single-Center Study Highlighting the High Incidence of Complications Within 5 Years.
PMID:40937874.snippet:
Background

Congenital biliary dilatation (CBD) is a rare anomaly often treated surgically, yet postoperative complications remain a concern. This study aimed to evaluate the incidence, timing, and risk factors of such complications after CBD surgery.

Methods

A retrospective review was conducted on 184 patients with CBD who underwent either open or laparoscopic surgery, with a mean follow-up of 9 years. The analysis focused on postoperative complications, including bile duct-related issues, pancreatic complications, and bowel obstruction.

PMID:40968256.title: Safety and efficacy of robot-assisted bile ductoplasty and intrapancreatic bile duct resection in congenital biliary dilatation: a single-center retrospective cohort (2013-2024).
PMID:40968256.snippet: Robot-assisted surgery is increasingly being utilized for congenital biliary dilatation (CBD); however, limited data exist on its feasibility across age groups, particularly for bile ductoplasty and intrapancreatic bile duct (IPBD) resection. This was a retrospective cohort study that compared the outcomes of robot-assisted versus laparoscopic CBD surgery in 159 patients (Rob group: 57; Lap group: 102) treated between 2013 and 2024. PMID:41356644.title: Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma Masquerading as Liver Abscess: A Case Report With Multimodal Imaging.
PMID:41356644.snippet: The presentation of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) often masquerades as a pyogenic liver abscess. Therefore, atypical imaging features on multimodal studies, together with markedly elevated levels of Gamma-glutamyl Transpeptidase (GGT), Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) and Carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9), must alert clinicians to the possibility of underlying malignancy to prevent diagnostic delay.

PMID:40665446.title: Analysis of risk factors of cholangiocarcinoma, role of diabetes mellitus and hepatitis B virus infection in the intrahepatic and extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: a retrospective case-based study in China.
PMID:40665446.snippet:
Background

The cause and carcinogenesis of cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) remain unclear. In this study, we conducted a population-based case-control study in China to evaluate the effects of diabetes mellitus (DM), hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, and other potential risk factors for cholangiocarcinoma (CCA).

Methods

PMID:41912863.title: Circulating tumor DNA-based detection of molecular residual disease in isocitrate dehydrogenase-mutant cholangiocarcinoma for biomarker-guided therapy.
PMID:41912863.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), particularly the IDH-mutant subtype, presents major clinical challenges because it is frequently diagnosed at an advanced stage and carries a high risk of postoperative recurrence. Detecting minimal residual disease (MRD) is crucial, as it enables early identification of patients at high risk of relapse, guiding personalized adjuvant therapy to prevent recurrence and improve survival. PMID:41873318.title: Integrating Circulating Tumor DNA (ctDNA) Into Postoperative Surveillance After the Resection of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: A Proposed Hybrid Imaging-Molecular Framework.
PMID:41873318.snippet: Recurrence after curative-intent resection remains common in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) and continues to limit long-term survival. Although repeat liver resection may benefit carefully selected patients, this opportunity is often lost because recurrence is detected only after radiographic progression. Postoperative surveillance relies primarily on cross-sectional imaging, which performs well for macroscopic disease but lacks sensitivity for microscopic residual tumor. PMID:42145022.title: Advances and applications of liquid biopsy approaches in hepatopancreatobiliary (HPB) cancers: a literature review.
PMID:42145022.snippet:
Background and objective

Hepatopancreatobiliary (HPB) cancers, including pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), are among the deadliest malignancies due to late-stage diagnosis and limited curative options. Conventional tissue biopsies are often invasive and insufficient for longitudinal monitoring. This review synthesizes the current available literature on liquid biopsy, a minimally invasive approach that uses analysis of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in serum, plasma, or bile, to enable better early detection, surveillance, and treatment monitoring of HPB cancers.

PMID:41955548.snippet:

Hepatopancreatobiliary (HPB) cancers-including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), and gallbladder cancer-are aggressive malignancies with limited treatment options and poor prognosis. PMID:42122131.title: Integrating Advanced Endoscopic Techniques and Confocal Microscopy for Early Detection of Extrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:42122131.snippet: Extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (eCCA) is a highly aggressive malignancy arising from the biliary epithelium, with surgical resection representing the only potentially curative treatment. PMID:40689505.snippet:

PMID:41866828.title: Liquid biopsy biomarkers for early detection of gastrointestinal cancers: Current landscape and emerging technologies.
PMID:41866828.snippet: Early detection of gastrointestinal (GI) cancers remains a critical unmet clinical need, as most patients are diagnosed at advanced stages when prognosis is poor. PMID:41095804.title: Point-of-Care Testing and Biomarkers in Biliary Diseases: Current Evidence and Future Directions.

PMID:41919759.title: Clonorchis sinensis and cholangiocarcinoma: molecular mechanisms and biomarker advances.
PMID:41919759.snippet: Clonorchis sinensis, a common food-borne liver fluke in East Asia, is a Group 1 carcinogen strongly linked to cholangiocarcinoma. PMID:42165910.snippet: Biliary tract cancer (BTC) is typically diagnosed at an advanced stage due to the lack of effective screening tools, resulting in limited therapeutic options and poor survival outcomes. PMID:41559763.title: Novel Liquid Biopsy in Gastrointestinal Cancers.
PMID:41559763.snippet: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers represent a significant global health burden, being among the leading causes of cancer-related deaths. The prognosis for patients remains unsatisfactory, largely because most cancers are detected at advanced stages. PMID:41652428.snippet: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and biliary tract cancers (BTCs) are characterized by dismal prognoses, largely because effective strategies for early detection are lacking and post-surgical relapse is common. PMID:41883993.title: Circulating Tumor DNA in Cholangiocarcinoma: A Precision Oncology Roadmap.
PMID:41883993.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a rare but aggressive malignancy with a rising global incidence and few therapeutic options for advanced disease. In recent decades, precision oncology for CCA has advanced rapidly, particularly through the development of targeted therapies for patients with actionable genetic alterations. These therapies have markedly prolonged survival and improved other clinical outcomes among patients with unresectable, advanced CCA. The implementation of precision oncology largely depends on detecting genetic mutations to guide patient selection and treatment, using tumor tissue biopsies or liquid biopsies, including circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) from blood or bile. OT:MONDO_0019087.title: cholangiocarcinoma (disease)
OT:MONDO_0019087.snippet: A carcinoma that arises from the intrahepatic biliary tree (intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma) or from the junction, or adjacent to the junction, of the right and left hepatic ducts (hilar cholangiocarcinoma). Grossly, the malignant lesions are solid, nodular, and grayish. Morphologically, the vast majority of cases are adenocarcinomas. Signs and symptoms include malaise, weight loss, right upper quadrant abdominal pain, and night sweats. Early detection is difficult and the prognosis is generally poor.

PMID:39944751.snippet: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a rare cholestatic liver disease, characterised by persistent biliary inflammation resulting in fibrosis and multifocal strictures of the biliary tree. PMID:37770126.title: British Society of Gastroenterology guidelines for the diagnosis and management of cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:37770126.snippet: These guidelines for the diagnosis and management of cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) were commissioned by the British Society of Gastroenterology liver section. The guideline writing committee included a multidisciplinary team of experts from various specialties involved in the management of CCA, as well as patient/public representatives from AMMF (the Cholangiocarcinoma Charity) and PSC Support. Quality of evidence is presented using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation (AGREE II) format. The recommendations arising are to be used as guidance rather than as a strict protocol-based reference, as the management of patients with CCA is often complex and always requires individual patient-centred considerations.

OT:MONDO_0006180.title: digestive system adenoma (disease)
OT:MONDO_0006180.snippet: A sporadic or less frequently familial neoplasm, arising from the glandular epithelium of the stomach, small intestine, biliary tract, colon, and rectum. It is a polypoid or flat circumscribed lesion. Morphologically, it is characterized by a proliferation of neoplastic glandular cells and it is associated with dysplasia. According to the growth pattern, it may be classified as tubular, villous, or tubulovillous. The dysplasia is classified as mild, moderate, or severe. The frequency of malignant transformation depends on the size of the lesion and the degree of dysplasia. Larger adenomas with severe dysplastic changes (sometimes called carcinoma in situ) carry a higher risk of progressing to invasive adenocarcinoma. Gastrointestinal adenomas may present as solitary or multifocal lesions.

Given the limited therapeutic options and poor prognoses for patients with advanced-stage disease, there is an urgent and unmet clinical need for novel targeted therapies. Cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibitors (such as palbociclib, ribociclib, and abemaciclib) exert their effects by arresting the cell cycle at the G1/S checkpoint. PMID:41692706.snippet:
Background

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most aggressive cancers, typically diagnosed at an advanced stage due to its subtle and often absent early symptoms. Despite representing only 3% of new cancer cases, it is projected to become the second leading cause of cancer-related deaths by 2030. Currently, early diagnosis remains a significant challenge, and survival rates remain poor due to the lack of effective screening tools.

Methods

We conducted a comprehensive literature review to explore the most recent advances in PDAC detection, focusing on novel biomarkers, liquid biopsies, artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced imaging, and non-invasive surveillance strategies. PMID:40959208.title: Transforming Cancer Diagnostics: The Emergence of Liquid Biopsy and Epigenetic Markers.
PMID:40959208.snippet: Liquid biopsy represents a transformative approach in oncology, enabling noninvasive disease detection and monitoring through epigenetic signals in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), nucleosomes, and noncoding RNAs. Tumor initiation is driven by epigenetic modifications, including DNA methylation, histone alterations, and dysregulated noncoding RNAs, which disrupt gene regulation, cell cycle control, DNA repair, and metastatic processes. This review systematically examines recent evidence on DNA methylation, histone marks (e.g., H3K27me3, H3K18ac), and noncoding RNAs (miRNAs, lncRNAs) as biomarkers for early cancer detection, prognosis, and therapeutic response. PMID:41178912.title: Global gene expression landscape of gallbladder cancer and advances in targeted therapeutic strategies.
PMID:41178912.snippet: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) is a lethal biliary tract malignancy, which is infrequent in most developed countries, but common in many developing countries in specific geographical regions of the world. Non-specific symptoms leading to late diagnosis is one of the primary factors contributing to poor prognosis in GBC. An understanding of the complex relationship between molecular genetics and epidemiological variances in the incidence rates of GBC is thus of utmost importance. CIVIC:EID7638.snippet:
A patient with cholangiocarcinoma harboring with ERBB2 amplification (3+) detected by circulating tumor DNA testing and confirmed by tissue-based testing was treated with trastuzumab and pertuzumab.
This treatment showed a tumor response and continued over 12 months.

This study will combine the use of a fluorescent-labeled peptide dimer that binds specifically to know biomarkers of cholangiocarcinoma for use as a novel imaging agent to guide endoscopic biopsies. This Phase 1B study will be used to provide early evidence of efficacy for the topical application of a peptide dimer that binds to molecular targets that are specific for biliary intra-epithelial neoplasia. CT:NCT07194057.title: "A Privacy-protecting Environment for Child Transplants Health Related and Genomic Data Integration in the European Reference Network"
CT:NCT07194057.snippet:
Protect\_Child\_101 is an observational study to be performed in children that have undergone a liver or renal transplant.

The aim of this study is to analyse small variations in the genetic material (DNA) of transplanted children. The investigators will also study a type of chemical 'marks' called methylations, which do not change the DNA itself, but can affect how it functions. These marks can influence how certain diseases develop or how the body responds to transplantation.

Specifically, investigators seek to discover:

* Whether there are genetic or epigenetic (methylation) alterations that may explain why some children develop serious diseases that require transplantation.

CT:NCT07205874.title: Early Diagnosis of Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC) in Patients With Positive Anti-Mitochondrial Antibodies (AMA) and Normal Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP)
CT:NCT07205874.snippet:
The goal of this observational study is to achieve early diagnosis of Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC) in patients with positive Anti-Mitochondrial Antibodies (AMA) and Normal Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) in adults aged 18-80 years with positive AMA and normal ALP. The main question it aims to answer is:

• Are there any predictive factors for histological PBC in patients with positive AMA and normal ALP? Participants will undergo a liver biopsy and specific blood tests if eligible based on inclusion and exclusion criteria.

CT:NCT03041662.title: Surveillance Study for Early Detection of Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) in Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC)
CT:NCT03041662.snippet: This observational study of a national cohort of 600 Swedish PSC patients include yearly MR/MRCP, biobanking of serum, plasma and blood, followup clinical data (interventions, symptoms, labs, colonoscopy). The aim is to collect a well characterized cohort of PSC patients and provide future possibilities to evaluate biomarkers for prognosis and early cancer detection.

CT:NCT07454486.snippet:
Purpose of the Study:

Bile duct cancers are rare and aggressive. About 250 new cases are diagnosed each year in Denmark. These cancers are difficult to detect early, so only about 20% of patients can have surgery when diagnosed. Even after surgery, the cancer often returns, and chemotherapy only slightly reduces the risk of relapse.

For patients who cannot have surgery, treatments such as chemotherapy (sometimes combined with immunotherapy) can relieve symptoms and extend life, but their effect is limited. A small number of patients have specific genetic changes in their cancer that can be treated with targeted medicines.

PMID:33579427.title: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: Morpho-molecular pathology, tumor reactive microenvironment, and malignant progression.
PMID:33579427.snippet: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is a relatively rare, but highly lethal and biologically complex primary biliary epithelial cancer arising within liver. After hepatocellular carcinoma, iCCA is the second most common primary liver cancer, accounting for approximately 10-20% of all primary hepatic malignancies. Over the last 10-20 years, iCCA has become the focus of increasing concern largely due to its rising incidence and high mortality rates in various parts of the world, including the United States. The challenges posed by iCCA are daunting and despite recent progress in the standard of care and management options for iCCA, the prognosis for this cancer continues to be dismal. PMID:42373229.snippet:
Background/aim

Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) has a poor prognosis, partly due to late diagnosis and limited efficacy of systemic therapies. Gemcitabine remains a commonly used chemotherapeutic agent for CCA; however, the clinical response is heterogeneous, and predictive biomarkers are lacking. Although epigenetic regulators have been implicated in gemcitabine sensitivity in other malignancies, their relevance in CCA has not been explored systematically. This study aimed to identify epigenetic candidates associated with the gemcitabine response in CCA and to validate their functional role.

PMID:42015571.snippet:
Introduction

Differentiating between malignant and benign biliary strictures remains a clinical challenge because current diagnostic tools have limited sensitivity. The detection of tumour-related biomarkers directly in bile, which is in close contact with the lesion, may enhance diagnostic accuracy. This study aimed at evaluating the diagnostic and prognostic values of biliary concentrations of VEGF, PDGF-AA, IGF and MMPs in patients with extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), or benign obstruction.

Methods

PMID:42286359.title: Emerging omics diagnosis of perihilar cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:42286359.snippet: Perihilar cholangiocarcinoma (pCCA) frequently presents as an indeterminate perihilar biliary stricture. The diagnosis is often delayed or uncertain because of the limited sensitivity of conventional endobiliary sampling and blood-based markers, especially in patients with additional confounding conditions such as primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). This diagnostic ambiguity can significantly impact clinical outcomes as timely detection and accurate classification are critical for referral and curative-intent treatment. As such, research focused on advancing diagnostic methodologies is a priority. pCCA has a distinct proteomic signature, pattern of activated signaling cascades, epigenetic modifications, and metabolic interactions within its anatomic niche. PMID:42067191.snippet:
Background & aims

Current methods for cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) detection in primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) lack accuracy, often leading to late, non-curative diagnoses. In this study, we aim at identifying DNA methylation biomarkers in liquid biopsies for earlier and more accurate CCA detection.

Methods

After droplet digital PCR assay development, quality control, and verification in tissue, we selected four biomarkers for evaluation in bile (n = 272) and plasma (n = 128) samples from individuals with PSC and/or CCA collected across three different hospitals.

PMID:42313299.title: Pharmacokinetic modelling of MRI-based liver function for risk assessment in primary sclerosing cholangitis: a prospective pilot study.
PMID:42313299.snippet:
Objective

Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a rare fibroinflammatory hepatobiliary disease with a highly variable clinical course. Identifying patients at risk for poor outcomes remains challenging. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based approaches such as DiStrict, Anali score, and relative enhancement (RE) show promise but are limited by operator dependency or static measurements. This study explored pharmacokinetic modelling of liver function as a quantitative imaging biomarker for risk assessment in PSC.

PMID:42123212.title: Beyond the Graft: Optimizing Post-Transplant Care in Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
PMID:42123212.snippet: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by fibro-inflammatory lesions of the biliary tree. In the absence of available, effective medical therapies, many patients progress to liver failure, making PSC one of the leading indications for liver transplantation (LT), despite its rarity. While LT in PSC is associated with good overall short- and long-term survival, post-transplant outcomes are limited by recurrent PSC (rPSC), which affects up to one quarter of PSC recipients with a significant risk of graft loss and re-transplantation. PMID:42112333.title: Case Report: A steroid-sparing mechanical management of IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis mimicking cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:42112333.snippet:
Background

IgG4-SC typically requires long-term corticosteroid therapy. We report a distinctive case of a 65-year-old woman with biopsy-supported IgG4-SC that closely mimicked malignancy.

Case summary

The patient presented with 10 kg weight loss and CA19-9 of 315 U/mL. She achieved sustained clinical and biochemical remission after repeated endoscopic mechanical decompression alone, with no recurrent obstructive cholestasis during long-term clinical and biochemical follow-up. However, serum IgG4 remained elevated at long-term reassessment, and complete immunologic remission could not be assumed.

PMID:40996984.title: A circulating microRNA panel enhances the diagnosis of cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:40996984.snippet:
Background and aim

Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), a malignancy with a high incidence in regions endemic for the liver fluke Opisthorchis viverrini, is frequently characterized by alterations in the p53 tumor-suppressor gene, a process often modulated by microRNAs. Our study aimed to identify circulating miRNAs as potential diagnostic biomarkers for CCA.

Methods

We sequenced small RNAs to identify differentially expressed microRNAs (miRNAs) in two CCA cell lines (one p53-mutant, one p53-wildtype) relative to an immortalized cholangiocyte cell line. Candidate miRNAs exhibiting significant upregulation with a log2 fold change > 4.5 were selected for validation via RT-qPCR in serum samples from patients with CCA. PMID:42326456.title: Ileal Bile Acid Transporter Inhibitors for Symptomatic Cholestasis due to Vanishing Bile Duct Syndrome in Adults.
PMID:42326456.snippet: Vanishing bile duct syndrome (VBDS) is a rare cholangiopathy that may follow drug-induced liver injury and can progress to liver failure. No established pharmacological treatment is currently available. We present a case of a 65-year-old man diagnosed with histologically confirmed and progressive symptomatic VBDS, probably sustained by drug-induced liver injury, who was successfully treated with a 4-week course of off-label ileal bile acid transporter inhibitor treatment of the management of pruritus. To our knowledge, this is among the first reports of successful ileal bile acid transporter inhibitor use in VBDS. PMID:41884039.title: Neonatal cholestasis is associated with cytochrome P450 1A2 detoxification defect: A single center pilot study.
PMID:41884039.snippet:
Background

Evidence supports that biliary atresia (BA) in Egyptian infants is an aflatoxin-induced cholangiopathy acquired perinatally in infants with glutathione S-transferase M1 deficiency: The Kotb disease BA variant. This inability to detoxify aflatoxins leads to progressive inflammatory adhesions and obliterative cholangiopathy early in life.

Aim

To investigate the cytochrome P450 1A2 (CYP1A2) detoxification enzyme levels in neonates with confirmed BA.

Methods

This prospective descriptive analytical study estimated CYP1A2 detoxification enzyme levels using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in 20 neonates with confirmed BA. The level CYP1A2 was also estimated in a control group of 20 infants with neonatal hepatitis (NH) and 20 age- and sex-matched healthy infants.

PMID:42257007.snippet: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) remains a diagnosis of exclusion and requires systematic causality assessment. Meropenem is generally considered hepatically safe; however, rare cases of idiosyncratic DILI have been reported. We describe a 33-year-old female who developed progressive elevation of liver tests following exposure to meropenem. Based on R-value calculation, the liver injury pattern was mixed at presentation and peak, with transient hepatocellular features followed by evolution toward a cholestatic pattern during recovery. PMID:40977641.snippet:
Background

Steroid-refractory immune-related cholangitis, characterized by biliary obstruction, can be caused by drugs such as immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). PMID:42311264.title: Case Report: Response to ivosidenib in patients with cholangiocarcinoma: a clinical perspective with illustrative cases.
PMID:42311264.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a rare cancer, rich in molecular targets. Molecular targeted therapy is the recommended second-line approach for patients with advanced or metastatic CCA, including ivosidenib for patients with mutations in the gene for isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1). PMID:41891998.snippet: Objectives: The TNM staging system for distal cholangiocarcinoma (dCCA) has limited accuracy due to its anatomical basis. Methods: We analyzed 208 dCCA patients undergoing pancreaticoduodenectomy (2017-2024). PMID:41008833.title: Type 2 Diabetes and Gastrointestinal Cancers: Risk Associations and Awareness of Screening Challenges.
PMID:41008833.snippet:
Objectives

Type 2 diabetes (T2D) has been increasingly associated with a heightened risk of various gastrointestinal (GI) cancers. This narrative review aims to synthesise current evidence on the link between newly diagnosed T2D and GI malignancies, and to propose a clinical framework for risk-adapted cancer vigilance.

Methods

We conducted a narrative review of the literature focusing on the association between T2D and GI cancers, including colorectal, pancreatic, liver, gastric, and biliary malignancies. We examined shared risk factors, underlying biological mechanisms, and emerging insights into pathophysiology.

Immune dysfunction, systemic inflammation, and malnutrition are closely associated with tumor progression and prognosis in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC). This multicenter retrospective study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of immune-inflammatory-nutritional biomarkers and to establish a novel cholangiocarcinoma immune-inflammatory-nutritional score (CIINS).

Methods

A total of 284 ICC patients who underwent curative surgical resection at three medical centers were retrospectively analyzed and divided into a training cohort (n = 182) and a validation cohort (n = 102). PMID:40870842.snippet: Type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis (AIP), IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis (IgG4-SC), and IgG4-related cholecystitis are recognized as IgG4-related pancreatobiliary diseases. ERCP-guided brush cytology has been the long-standing tissue-sampling strategy, but its reported sensitivity for malignancy is limited, frequently falling below 50% in published series. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) remains central to the diagnosis of CCA and management of PSC-related complications. This review synthesizes current evidence guiding the use of ERCP in patients with PSC, highlighting the importance of careful patient selection to mitigate adverse events. PMID:40164585.title: Leveraging glycosylation for early detection and therapeutic target discovery in pancreatic cancer.
PMID:40164585.snippet: Pancreatic cancer (PC) remains one of the most lethal malignancies, primarily due to late-stage diagnosis, limited biomarker specificity, and aggressive metastatic potential. Recent glycoproteomic studies have illuminated the crucial role of glycosylation in PC progression, revealing altered glycosylation patterns that impact cell adhesion, immune evasion, and tumor invasiveness. PMID:38486989.title: The role of <i>N</i>-glycosylation in cancer.
PMID:38486989.snippet: Despite advances in understanding the development and progression of cancer in recent years, there remains a lack of comprehensive characterization of the cancer glycoproteome. Glycoproteins play an important role in medicine and are involved in various human disease conditions including cancer. Glycan-moieties participate in fundamental cancer processes like cell signaling, invasion, angiogenesis, and metastasis. Aberrant N-glycosylation significantly impacts cancer processes and targeted therapies in clinic. PMID:36072925.snippet: Glycosylation is one of the most important post-translational modifications (PTMs) in a protein, and is the most abundant and diverse biopolymer in nature. Glycans are involved in multiple biological processes of cancer initiation and progression, including cell-cell interactions, cell-extracellular matrix interactions, tumor invasion and metastasis, tumor angiogenesis, and immune regulation. As an important biomarker, tumor-associated glycosylation changes have been extensively studied. This article reviews recent advances in glycosylation-based biomarker research, which is useful for cancer diagnosis and prognostic assessment. PMID:38084450.snippet: The lack of efficient biomarkers for the early detection of gastric cancer (GC) contributes to its high mortality rate, so it is crucial to discover novel diagnostic targets for GC. PMID:41411373.title: Transcriptomics analysis of in vivo Opisthorchis viverrini: Stage-specific gene expression and novel genes with stable expression in mammalian stages for opisthorchiasis intervention.
PMID:41411373.snippet: Opisthorchis viverrini, Southeast Asian liver fluke, is a parasitic flatworm that has been widely spread in Asia and is a major risk factor for bile duct cancer - cholangiocarcinoma (CCA). PMID:41339391.title: Machine learning approach using electrochemical immunosensor data for precise classification of Opisthorchis viverrini infection.
PMID:41339391.snippet: Opisthorchiasis, a major foodborne parasitic zoonotic disease in Thailand and neighboring countries, is caused by the carcinogenic liver fluke Opisthorchis viverrini (OV). Accurate classification of OV infection is critical for timely intervention and public health management. In this study, we propose a reliable machine learning (ML) classification model based on peak current data from an electrochemical immunosensor and additional patient condition features, which can facilitate intuitive decision-making without the need for expert personnel. PMID:40595543.title: Immunomics-guided biomarker discovery for human liver fluke infection and infection-associated cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:40595543.snippet: Sensitive diagnostics are needed to improve management and surveillance of opisthorchiasis and opisthorchiasis-associated cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) throughout East Asia. PMID:41379246.title: Omics-enhanced nanomedicine: integrating multi-omics for precision cancer diagnosis and therapy.
PMID:41379246.snippet: Cancer nanomedicine has emerged as a transformative approach in oncology, providing targeted therapeutic strategies with enhanced efficacy and reduced systemic toxicity. PMID:40229491.title: Identification of serum metabolite biomarkers and metabolic reprogramming mechanisms to predict recurrence in cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:40229491.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) has high recurrence rates that severely limit long-term survival. Effective tools for accurate recurrence monitoring and diagnosis remain lacking. This study aimed to identify metabolite-based biomarkers to evaluate recurrence severity, enhance disease management, and elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying CCA recurrence. PMID:40857390.title: Integrating multi-omics in bile for biomarker discovery in cholangiocarcinoma.

Background

PMID:41097793.title: Advanced Biliary Tract Cancer: Exploration of Third-Line and Other Therapeutic Areas After Failure of Chemotherapy Alone.
PMID:41097793.snippet: Biliary tract cancer (BTC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with an extremely poor prognosis and a gradually increasing incidence, warranting increased clinical attention. However, due to disparities in medical resources and limited understanding of the disease, outcomes following first- and second-line therapies remain suboptimal. PMID:39103092.snippet: Cholangiocarcinomas (CCAs) are a heterogeneous group of malignant tumors that originate from the biliary tract. They are usually diagnosed in advanced stages, leading to a poor prognosis for affected patients. As CCA often arises as a sporadic cancer in individuals lacking specific risk factors or with heterogeneous backgrounds, and there are no defined high-risk groups, the implementation of effective surveillance programs for CCA is problematic. PMID:40723883.title: The Future of Tumor Markers: Advancing Early Malignancy Detection Through Omics Technologies, Continuous Monitoring, and Personalized Reference Intervals.
PMID:40723883.snippet: Malignant diseases represent a major global health challenge and are among the leading causes of death worldwide. Accurate early diagnosis is essential for improving outcomes and combating these conditions effectively. Currently, the diagnosis of malignancies relies heavily on radiological imaging and pathological examinations, which are often invasive and not cost-effective. As such, there is a growing need for non-invasive and accessible methods to detect cancer in its early stages. PMID:35582128.title: Novel approaches in search for biomarkers of cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:35582128.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) arises from the ductular epithelium of the biliary tree, either within the liver (intrahepatic CCA) or more commonly from the extrahepatic bile ducts (extrahepatic CCA). PMID:41676065.title: Microbial dysbiosis in cholangiocarcinoma.
PMID:41676065.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a highly aggressive malignancy of the biliary epithelium, with its incidence and mortality rates continuing to rise worldwide. PMID:42299582.title: Metagenomic profiling of biliary microbiota reveals distinct microbial and functional features in cholelithiasis and cholecystic polyps.

PMID:41178929.title: Circulating tumor DNA in biliary tract cancers: A review of current applications.
PMID:41178929.snippet: Molecular profiling of biliary tract cancers (BTCs) has paved the way for a broader range of therapeutic options, leading to improved survival outcomes. Given the challenges of tissue evaluation in BTCs, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has emerged as a promising non-invasive biomarker for genomic profiling. Bile has been proven to be a reliable ctDNA source, demonstrating higher concordance with tumor tissue than plasma. PMID:42180160.title: Investigation of the Intensity of Thrombocytosis as a Potential Prognostic Indicator in Canine Malignant Neoplasms.
PMID:42180160.snippet: Platelets contribute to cancer progression, and thrombocytosis is a recognized poor prognostic factor in human oncology; however, its significance in veterinary medicine remains underexplored. PMID:42077698.title: Platelet Mass Signatures and Thrombin-Activatable Fibrinolysis Inhibitor as Discriminators of Primary Thrombocytosis: Development of a Screening Algorithm in an Eastern Sudanese Cohort.
PMID:42077698.snippet:
Background

Clinically differentiating primary from reactive thrombocytosis is crucial, but it often requires expensive molecular and bone marrow examinations. Platelet indices and thrombosis-associated biomarkers may offer valuable diagnostic assistance.

Objective

This study aims to evaluate platelet indices and thrombin-activatable fibrinolysis inhibitor (TAFI) for discrimination between primary and reactive thrombocytosis and to develop a combined diagnostic model.

Methods

A cross-sectional analytical study included 74 Sudanese patients with thrombocytosis (29 primary and 45 reactive). Platelet indices and TAFI were measured. Diagnostic performance was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and multivariable logistic regression.

Background

This report assesses the feasibility of a sequential treatment strategy for a patient with active tuberculosis (TB) complicated by thrombocytosis and squamous cell lung carcinoma, involving initial anti-TB therapy combined with aspirin, followed by anticancer treatment. PMID:41795766.title: The role of hematological biomarkers as diagnostic tool in pre-cancerous patients.

Radiomics and artificial intelligence (AI) are progressively gaining recognition for predicting tumor response, recurrence, and prognosis in gastrointestinal tumors. The current review singled out the diagnostic and prognostic potential of AI and radiomics in the whole GI tract.

PMID:41695919.title: Deep learning in lower gastrointestinal cancer detection: Advances in endoscopic, radiologic, and histopathologic diagnostics.
PMID:41695919.snippet: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, particularly colorectal cancer, continue to be a major contributor to global cancer-related morbidity and mortality. PMID:37958227.title: Current and Emerging Strategies for Tubo-Ovarian Cancer Diagnostics.
PMID:37958227.snippet: Tubo-ovarian cancer is the most lethal gynaecological cancer. More than 75% of patients are diagnosed at an advanced stage, which is associated with poorer overall survival. Up to 80% of patients with resected pancreatic cancer experience recurrence within 2 years. We evaluated the feasibility and accuracy of a personalized, tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) test for the early detection of recurrence risk during long-term postoperative surveillance.

We recruited 43 patients with pancreatic cancer who underwent curative surgical resections. A personalized panel was developed to detect ctDNA in plasma based on whole-exome mutation information derived from tumor tissues. A total of 139 plasma samples were analyzed to assess recurrence risk and the efficacy of adjuvant therapy.

PPR:PPR1152614.snippet: Background Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) detects minimal residual disease (MRD) and predicts recurrence in resected colorectal cancer (CRC), with implications for adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) decision-making. Longitudinal ctDNA quantification and dynamics are less well studied. We present results from the ongoing prospective multi-centre TRACC study using a tumour-informed ctDNA assay. PMID:41346570.title: Personalized and Tumor Informed Circulating Tumor DNA Assay for Molecular Residual Disease Monitoring of Solid Malignancies.
PMID:41346570.snippet: Emerging evidence suggests that minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring in solid tumors has implications for prognosis, treatment response, and therapeutic intervention. However, detecting MRD requires highly sensitive and specific circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) assays. Therefore, we developed an innovative MRD monitoring assay that offers superior performance and cost advantage. PMID:42183187.title: Present and future of liver transplantation for cholangiocellular carcinoma: moving toward personalized multiparametric transplantability patterns.
PMID:42183187.snippet: Liver transplantation for cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) shifted from a contraindication to a promising therapeutic option for selected patients. Advances in neoadjuvant therapy and refined selection criteria resulted in long-term outcomes comparable to other accepted oncologic indications, particularly in perihilar CCA managed with standardized protocols and in intrahepatic CCA with favorable tumor biology. The future challenge is to develop a multiparametric biological selection, blending clinical, functional, histopathologic, molecular, and radiologic parameters to identify candidates with indolent disease behavior, thus maximizing oncologic benefit while ensuring appropriate use of limited graft resources.

PMID:42194537.title: Redefining Liver Transplantation Indications for Hepatic Malignancies in the Era of Precision Transplant Oncology: An Up-to-Date Narrative Review.
PMID:42194537.snippet: Background: Hepatic malignancies are a major global health burden, with rising incidence, high mortality, and frequent diagnosis at advanced or unresectable stages. Although surgical resection, locoregional therapies, and systemic treatments have improved outcomes, many patients remain ineligible for curative strategies because of tumor burden, anatomical constraints, or liver dysfunction. Liver transplantation (LT) has therefore evolved from a treatment limited to selected hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cases within strict morphological criteria to a broader oncologic option guided by tumor biology and treatment response. PMID:41675329.snippet:
Background and objective

Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers represent a substantial global health burden due to their high morbidity and mortality rates. These cancers are often diagnosed at advanced stages, leading to poor prognosis and limited treatment options. Early detection and personalized treatment strategies are critical to improving outcomes, yet traditional diagnostic methods, such as tissue biopsies and imaging, often fall short in sensitivity, specificity and the ability to capture tumor heterogeneity. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), which comprises small fragments of tumor-derived DNA shed into the bloodstream, has emerged as a transformative tool in the diagnosis and management of GI cancers. PMID:41992238.title: The evolving role of OMICS in gastrointestinal tumor biology and clinical practice.
PMID:41992238.snippet: Due to late diagnosis, high molecular diversity, and limited response to therapeutic intervention, gastrointestinal (GI) cancers result in a considerable number of cancer-related deaths. Classic clinicopathological classification and single omics analysis fail to adequately convey the extensive biological complexity related to progression of disease, developed therapy resistance and recurrence of the disease. As a result, the recent introduction of integrated multi-omics including genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and spatial profiling as well as the emerging use of liquid biopsy is substantially reshaping our understanding of and clinical approach to GI cancers. PMID:40963813.title: Diagnosis of Perihilar Osteoclast Giant Cell Carcinoma in an Elderly Patient: A Report of Diagnostic Challenges Over Several Attempts.
PMID:40963813.snippet: Cholangiocarcinoma is a rare gastrointestinal malignancy with an annual incidence of 0.3 to 6 cases per 100,000, and, usually, it is reported as adenocarcinoma in about 95% of the cases. It can develop as a result of combination of genetic predispositions and various risk factors like but not limited to choledochal cysts, cholelithiasis/choledocholithiasis, yet its diagnosis is challenging due to difficulties in obtaining tissue for diagnosis. In this study, we present a challenging case in diagnosis that reveals undifferentiated carcinoma with osteoclast-like giant cells in the perihilar region of the bile duct.

PMID:40380811.title: Liver transplantation as a treatment for cancer: comprehensive review.
PMID:40380811.snippet:
Background

Liver transplantation for cancer indications has gained momentum in recent years. This review is intended to optimize the care setting of liver transplant candidates by highlighting current indications, technical aspects and barriers with available solutions to facilitate the guidance of available strategies for healthcare professionals in specialized centres.

Methods

A review of the most recent relevant literature was conducted for all the cancer indications of liver transplantation including colorectal cancer liver metastases, hilar cholangiocarcinoma, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, neuroendocrine tumours, hepatocellular carcinoma and hepatic epitheloid haemangioendothelioma.

PMID:34733408.snippet: Biliary stenosis may represent a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge resulting in a delay in diagnosis and initiation of therapy due to the frequent difficulty in distinguishing a benign from a malignant stricture.
